outcome_ro: IDLE nu este imposibil după EOF: stop() revine fără schimbare când process=None și nu există settings_command/model close. Pentru un Host realmente nefolosit, IDLE/drained/0/0 este tocmai rezultatul normal după drain+close. În schimb, STOPPED/0/0 nu este o stare produsă de aceste căi și clientul existent o refuză. Nu înlocuim o precondiție presupus imposibilă cu alta imposibilă. Problema reală este observarea: status revendică owner_writer, iar EOF execută Stop; nu există un status+close general no-effect. Builderul și installerul existente pot fi reutilizate ca mecanisme de artefact, dar nu pot instala alt supervisor peste UI9 fără o extensie reală și verificată a pinningului/atestării. Nu recomand un nou subsystem sau owner.

facts: RuntimeHost starts state=IDLE, generation=0, epoch=0, process=None, peer=None, capabilities={}.
Every authenticated _handle finalizer invokes stop(); the supervisor finally invokes runtime.drain(), then runtime.close(). Neither call alone implies state=STOPPED.

stop() first revokes the management lifeline. Under stop_lock, an already STOPPED Host returns. With process=None and no model close or settings_command, it returns without assigning state: pristine IDLE stays IDLE, including after owner disconnect.

If a settings command was accepted, generation/epoch are bound before MANAGEMENT. A cancelled or failed management startup can yield STOPPED even with process=None, but its epoch is nonzero. A native launch also binds the fence before process creation; successful drain does not reset it.
The internal MANAGEMENT-to-model transition sets IDLE temporarily but does not reset its bound fence. It is not a fresh no-work Host and cannot satisfy strict IDLE/0/0.

snapshot.drained is a projection of state in {IDLE,STOPPED}, not a separate live process census. Under normal source transitions a zero-fence IDLE Host has never accepted launch or Settings; installed provenance and original boot/resource identity still have to be attested.

RuntimeClient accepts zero-fence only when state=IDLE. Every other state must match the client's generation/epoch; its constructor requires epoch>=1. Merely adding STOPPED/0/0 to a prose contract cannot work through the existing client.
